clue.text: Greek hero attains eminence amongst those who excel

indicators.note: amongst says the high ground sits in the middle of the top performers

parts.note: aces are people who excel at something
an eminence is a piece of rising ground, a hill

explanation.surface: A Greek champion rises to prominence among the very best.
explanation.definitionFit: The warrior of Homer's Iliad is the foremost hero of Greek legend.

clue.text: Protection of right to be in love

indicators.note: to be in puts the letter for right within the word for love

parts.note: amour is a love affair, from French

explanation.surface: Defending one's right to fall in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Armour is a protective covering, such as a knight's metal suit.

clue.text: Drunk on Adam's ale from Lake Titicaca, perhaps

parts.note: high means intoxicated
Adam's ale is a jocular name for plain water

explanation.surface: Tipsy on nothing stronger than lake water from the Andes.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Titicaca, in the Andes, is one of the highest navigable lakes in the world, hence an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The lake lies some 3,800 metres up, making it lofty water indeed.

clue.text: King Edward gets found out

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king
Ned is a familiar form of Edward

explanation.surface: A royal Edward is discovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned means discovered, as in learning the truth.

clue.text: They are paradoxical odds

parts.note: betting odds of one to one carry a name meaning the opposite of odd numbers, hence the paradox

explanation.definitionFit: Even money odds, a one-to-one bet, are named for the numbers that oddness excludes.

clue.text: Volcanic mount presents oriental puzzle

parts.note: E, for east, is the oriental direction
a rebus is a picture puzzle

explanation.surface: A volcano offers an Eastern riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Erebus is the active volcano on Ross Island in Antarctica.

clue.text: Told mounting account is overdrawn

indicators.note: is reads as 'is in' the colour of debt, so the account sits within that word

parts.note: an overdrawn bank account is in the red

indicators.note: mounting, in a down entry, says the word for account rises and reads backwards

parts.note: a tale is an account or story

explanation.surface: A rising bank balance turns out to be in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns TALE to ELAT; an account that is overdrawn is in the red, so ELAT goes inside RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Related means narrated, as one relates a story.

clue.text: Stand around, left in fog

indicators.note: around says the word for stand encloses the letter for left

parts.note: to bear is to stand or tolerate

explanation.surface: Someone waits about, stranded in the mist.
explanation.definitionFit: Blear means dim and blurred of sight, as when lost in a haze.

clue.text: Enchanting letter writing

definitions.meaning: putting letters in the right order to form words

explanation.surface: A love letter so charming it bewitches.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both bewitching with a charm and the correct forming of words from letters.

clue.text: Lancashire town has one — a general assembly

parts.note: Eccles is a town near Manchester, historically in Lancashire, famous for its currant cakes
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A northern town boasts a single big public meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Athens the ecclesia was the popular assembly of citizens.

clue.text: Egg deal local men hammer out in Oxford

indicators.note: to hammer out is to beat into a new shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Villagers bash out a bargain over eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hammer out' rearranges EGG DEAL LOCAL MEN; the definition is only a hint of place, since the answer is one of the colleges in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Magdalen is one of the constituent colleges of the University of Oxford, so it is found there.

clue.text: Part of the orchestra in a French symphony initially relaxes

parts.note: un is the French for a
the wind is the section of an orchestra that blows its instruments

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word symphony

explanation.surface: Wind players in a French symphony start to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind is to loosen up after tension, an idiom for winding down.

clue.text: Shoot Capone after — not now

indicators.note: after places the gangster's name behind the word for not now

parts.note: later means at some future time, not now
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: Gun down Capone, but leave it till later.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a lateral is a side branch growing from a main stem.

clue.text: Being of a thoughtful nature suits duo perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Two people of a reflective temperament are well matched.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bookish is inclined to reflection and diligent study.

clue.text: Exit is said to be more important

indicators.note: is said signals that the phrase for an exit is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a way out, here phrased as out way, is an exit

explanation.surface: Leaving matters more than anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The exit, 'out way', said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To outweigh is to exceed in importance, from tipping a balance.

clue.text: Strained to portray knight

parts.note: to draw is to portray in a picture
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An artist struggles to paint a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn face looks tense and tired, as if pulled tight.

clue.text: Arrival by river an exciting experience

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Turning up beside a river makes for a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is a daring, thrilling episode.

clue.text: Could be in a team, but not probable

definitions.text: in a team, but not probable
definitions.meaning: in a sports trial match the ... play the stronger Probables

explanation.surface: A player might make the side, but it is unlikely.
explanation.walkthrough: In British trial matches (rugby especially) the 'Probables' team faces the 'Possibles', the less likely picks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means feasible and also names a player in the weaker side of a trial match.

clue.text: Iris's embroidery

definitions.meaning: read as 'iris is': an iris, especially its fragrant root
a lace worked in gold or silver thread

explanation.surface: Iris has taken up needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a scented plant and a gold-and-silver lace used for trimming garments.

clue.text: The sort of good example that may be illuminating

definitions.text: The sort of good example that may be illuminating

parts.words: The sort of good example that may be illuminating
parts.note: a model of excellence is described by the same word as a lamp giving out light

explanation.definitionFit: A glowing lamp and an outstanding model are both described by this word.

clue.text: A booklet I possess to do with drawing

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet or booklet
I've, short for I have, means I possess

explanation.surface: Someone owns a pamphlet about sketching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests sketching but means pulling, as a tractor draws a load.
explanation.definitionFit: Tractive describes pulling force, as in the traction of a locomotive hauling a load.

clue.text: Make Hardy go then — you sound terrible

indicators.note: terrible says the letters are in a dreadful mess and must be sorted

parts.note: U is pronounced like the word you

explanation.surface: Telling the novelist Hardy to get going, though his voice is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges GO THEN plus U, the letter that sounds like 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: To toughen is to harden or make robust.

clue.text: A right heartless man in the supply vessel

indicators.note: heartless takes away the central letter of the name

parts.note: Terry is a man's name

explanation.surface: A good but unfeeling man aboard a supply ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle R of TERRY, leaving TERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Arteries are blood vessels that carry supply from the heart.

clue.text: Yearn to get you and me back to the religious point

indicators.note: back says the pronoun for you and me is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: us means you and me
a spire is the pointed top of a church

explanation.surface: Longing to return together to the church steeple.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspire is to sigh, an old poetic word for longing.

clue.text: Roughly grips the branch

indicators.note: roughly says the letters are handled carelessly and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily grabs the bough.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small twig or shoot.

clue.text: Anaesthetic dish

definitions.meaning: something that knocks one out, like a stun gun
slang for a very attractive person

explanation.surface: A dish served in an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: One word serves for a thing that knocks a person senseless and for a strikingly good-looking person.

clue.text: Sinful creature?

parts.note: an animal sharing its name with one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.definitionFit: The slow tree-dwelling mammal shares its name with the deadly sin of laziness.

clue.text: Bertie building an arts centre (but not in Bow)

definitions.text: Bertie building an arts centre (but not in Bow)

parts.words: Bertie building an arts centre (but not in Bow)
parts.note: the music-hall song character Burlington Bertie came 'from Bow'; his namesake building is the London home of the Royal Academy of Arts, nowhere near Bow

explanation.surface: A man named Bertie puts up a gallery, though not in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlington Bertie from Bow is a famous music-hall song; Bow is a district in London's East End. The Piccadilly mansion sharing his name houses the Royal Academy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Piccadilly mansion is the headquarters of the Royal Academy of Arts.

clue.text: Employ, say, a girl no end stuck up

indicators.note: stuck up says the whole run is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

indicators.note: no end drops the final letter of the name

parts.note: Agnes is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Hire, for instance, a hopelessly snooty young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: AGNES loses its last letter to AGNE; EG + AGNE is EGAGNE, which 'stuck up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone is to hire them, a synonym of employ.

clue.text: Court risk by the railway

parts.note: to chance something is to risk it

explanation.surface: Flirting with danger beside the tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancery Division is a branch of the English High Court.
